solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: The last thing batter needs to stop collapse? (8)

annotation.definition: The last thing batter needs to stop collapse?

indicators.note: R plugs the gap in GO UNDER, as a stopper plugs a hole

annotation.surface: A baseball batter at the plate, desperate not to fail.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a grounder is a ball hit along the ground, easy to field and so the last thing a batter wants, and the last letter of batter sits inside GO UNDER.
annotation.definitionFit: A grounder in baseball is a ball hit along the ground, usually an easy out for the fielders.

entries.clue: “Meet” me on the waves? (5,3)

blocks.note: the surface reading: an invitation to a date, with waves as the open sea
the meant reading: the airwaves, where amateur broadcasters 'meet' only by voice

annotation.surface: An invitation to a rendezvous at sea.
annotation.walkthrough: The waves look like the sea, but they are airwaves: a radio ham is an amateur operator who 'meets' strangers only over the radio, hence the quotation marks.
annotation.definitionFit: A radio ham is a hobbyist who chats with other operators over the airwaves.

entries.clue: Ill-timed counter logic makes right arguments in the end (12)

indicators.note: the R is made into something else
the last letter of arguments

blocks.note: R = right, the letter to be replaced
last letter of argumentS, which takes R's place

annotation.surface: A debater's badly timed rebuttal leaves their argument right only at the close.
annotation.walkthrough: UNREASONABLE with its R swapped for S gives UNSEASONABLE, weather or remarks that come at the wrong time of year or moment.
annotation.definitionFit: Unseasonable means out of keeping with the season or occasion, so ill-timed.

entries.clue: The Cynic leaves us eating melon (8)

indicators.note: DIES takes OGEN inside it, like a mouth

blocks.note: Ogen is a variety of melon

annotation.surface: A sneering philosopher walks out mid-meal, still chewing melon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaves us' is a euphemism for dying. An Ogen is a small sweet melon, a crossword favourite for its letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Diogenes of Sinope was the most famous Cynic philosopher, the one said to have lived in a barrel.

entries.clue: Brought into line, book parts rather like Peter or Roger? (7)

indicators.note: the assembled letters are put inside RY
to part something is to split it, so B parts A BIT by sitting between its two words

annotation.surface: Book pages lined up neatly, perhaps with a note about two characters called Peter and Roger.
annotation.walkthrough: Two containers nest, one inside the other. Peter Rabbit and Roger Rabbit are the famous rabbits of Beatrix Potter and the film.
annotation.definitionFit: Peter Rabbit and Roger Rabbit are both rabbits, so being like them is rabbity.

entries.clue: A particular example is in this position (6)

indicators.note: INSTANCE is IN followed by the answer, so taking IN away leaves it

annotation.surface: A textbook remark that one example illustrates a point of view.
annotation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, the clue says INSTANCE is 'IN this', so this is STANCE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: your view on an issue is where you stand, and a boxer's footing is how they plant their feet.

entries.clue: Heritage group taken in by first-class con (4)

indicators.note: to be taken in is to be fooled, but also to be housed, and here NT is housed inside AI

blocks.note: A1 = first-class, the 1 read as I
the National Trust, the British body that looks after historic houses

annotation.surface: A conservation charity falls for a slick swindle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Con' looks like a swindle, but it is the opposite of pro, as in pros and cons.
annotation.definitionFit: A con is an argument against, and anti means against.

entries.clue: Show coppers curtains connected with front of theatre (8)

indicators.note: PENCE hangs either side of RE and T, like curtains round a stage

annotation.surface: Police officers draw the curtains at a theatre's front of house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' pretends to be police; here they are copper coins. 'Curtains' is a verb, the coins hanging either side of the other letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A show of feeling can be mere pretence, a false display.

entries.clue: What’s encapsulated by 007 and certain to stir? (8)

indicators.note: stirring mixes the letters, as Bond's martini is famously not

blocks.note: the character in the middle of 007, a zero read as the letter O

annotation.surface: James Bond, certain to cause a stir.
annotation.walkthrough: The O is what 007 encapsulates, the 0 held between the other two characters. A Bond film is the classic actioner, and the stir winks at shaken, not stirred.
annotation.definitionFit: An actioner is an action film, which is what every 007 outing is.

entries.clue: You did ask to ignore such a significant difference (4)

annotation.definitionNote: 'odds' is plural but works as the one difference, as in 'it makes no odds'

indicators.note: drop letters 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 of YOU DID ASK, the odd ones

blocks.note: the even letters: yOu DiD aSk

annotation.surface: A curt reply: you asked, so why pretend a big gap doesn't matter.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue teases its own mechanism: ignore the odd letters and the even ones spell ODDS.
annotation.definitionFit: Odds are the difference that decides things, as in 'it makes no odds' for no difference at all.

entries.clue: A breakfast order for one — Bill’s golf round ahead (4,8)

indicators.note: NEBS and G turn round to read GSBEN

blocks.note: a neb is a bill or beak, plus the 's
G = golf in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Someone orders breakfast just for themselves while Bill heads off for a round of golf.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Breakfast order' looks like a single phrase, but the definition stops at 'breakfast' and 'order' is EDICT. EG and the reversed NEBS plus G come 'ahead' of it.
annotation.definitionFit: Eggs Benedict, poached eggs and ham on a muffin with hollandaise, is a classic breakfast dish.

entries.clue: Ring done well, but individual characters adapted rhyme (4,4,4)

indicators.note: each word has just one letter changed

blocks.note: RING with R changed to D
DONE with E changed to G
WELL with W changed to B

annotation.surface: A bell rung well, with the letters of a verse altered.
annotation.walkthrough: Change one letter per word and 'Ring done well' becomes the nursery rhyme, the one where pussy's in the well, so the well survives in spirit.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Ding Dong Bell' is a traditional English nursery rhyme.

entries.clue: Select pipe to feed empty cistern (6)

indicators.note: HOSE goes into the cistern, as a pipe feeds a tank
CISTERN with its inside removed leaves C and N

blocks.note: a hose is a flexible pipe

annotation.surface: A plumbing instruction: choose a pipe to fill an empty water tank.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Select' looks like an imperative verb, but it is the adjective, as in a select few.
annotation.definitionFit: Select and chosen both mean picked out as the best.

entries.clue: Nothing loaded, in that case what’s charged magazine? (3,5)

indicators.note: THEN is loaded with O, carrying it inside

blocks.note: an ion is a charged particle

annotation.surface: A gun with nothing loaded, and a question about what the charge is.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loaded' and 'charged' dress the surface as firearms; one is a container signal, the other is chemistry.
annotation.definitionFit: The Onion is an American satirical news publication.

entries.clue: In the company of medic, dread takes hold (7)

indicators.note: ANGST takes hold of MO, gripping it inside

annotation.surface: Being around a doctor brings on a wave of fear.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads backwards from the surface: it is the dread that holds the medic, not the medic who causes the dread.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be among others is to be surrounded by them, in their midst.

entries.clue: Scales one of these when going over rising ground (3,5)

indicators.note: AS goes over, round the outside of, the scrambled RISING
RISING is ground up, reduced to scrambled bits

annotation.surface: A climber scales a slope, crossing a hill.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scales' looks like climbing, but it is Libra, the Scales, which with Gemini and Aquarius makes up the three air signs of the zodiac.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: astrology assigns Libra to the element air, alongside Gemini and Aquarius.

entries.clue: Relief only some deny donating to the West (7)

indicators.note: only some of the letters of 'deny donating' are used
going west in an across clue means reading right to left

blocks.note: dENY DONAting, the letters that read back as the answer

annotation.surface: Rich nations refusing aid to the West, leaving only a little relief.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like foreign aid politics; 'relief' is the painkilling kind.
annotation.definitionFit: An anodyne is a painkiller, something that brings relief.

entries.clue: Unaffiliated religious individual’s initiation in middle of day (8)

indicators.note: 'in' places one thing within another, so NUN and I sit within NOON

blocks.note: noon = the middle of the day
a religious = a member of a religious order, such as a nun

annotation.surface: A freelance believer is initiated at midday.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Religious' is a noun here: a religious is a monk or nun.
annotation.definitionFit: A nonunion worker is not affiliated to a trade union.

entries.clue: Having ruled out Holy Island, left with just an impression (8)

blocks.note: Iona, the Scottish island where St Columba founded his monastery

annotation.surface: Having struck a visit to a sacred island off the list, a traveller keeps only a vague memory of it.
annotation.walkthrough: Holy Island is also the name of Lindisfarne, which is the first island a solver may reach for; Iona is the other famous holy isle.
annotation.definitionFit: Something notional exists only as an idea or impression, not in reality.

entries.clue: Real life and natural laws are seen to grip (7)

annotation.definition2: Real life and natural laws are seen to

blocks.clueFragment: Real life and natural laws are seen to
blocks.note: read cryptically, the laws of nature are seen to hold for all of real life
a grip is an old word for a travelling bag

annotation.surface: A philosopher's remark that the laws of nature keep a firm grip on everyday life.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: natural laws are seen to HOLD for ALL of real life. 'Grip' is the noun, an old word for a travelling bag.
annotation.definitionFit: A grip is a holdall, a large soft bag for carrying clothes.

entries.clue: Film one crashing against tree, then reversed over (3,5)

indicators.note: I crashes into ARBOR, ending up inside it
V ARBOIR is turned back to front

blocks.note: arbor = tree in Latin, as in arboretum

annotation.surface: A film scene where someone crashes into a tree and then backs out.
annotation.walkthrough: The I goes inside ARBOR after V, the lot is reversed, and O is added last. Rio Bravo is a 1959 John Wayne western.
annotation.definitionFit: Rio Bravo is a Howard Hawks western starring John Wayne and Dean Martin.

entries.clue: On stage as temporary replacement? (6)

blocks.note: performing a role in a play
standing in for someone, as an interim manager does

annotation.surface: An understudy stepping onto the stage in someone else's place.
annotation.walkthrough: Both senses sit in the one picture: an understudy is on stage precisely as a temporary replacement.
annotation.definitionFit: Acting means performing on stage, and also serving temporarily, as an acting headmaster.

entries.clue: Compositions confirmed residents of Planet Earth? (6)

blocks.note: those confirmed as earthlings are certified as 'not' something: the negating prefix
ETs, extraterrestrials, are exactly what Earth's residents are not

annotation.surface: A question about songs written by people who are sure they are earthlings.
annotation.walkthrough: Split it as NON-ETS: anyone confirmed to live on Earth is not an ET, not an alien.
annotation.definitionFit: A nonet is a composition for nine players or voices.

entries.clue: “I H8 U”: slogan ultimately adopted by disaffected Biden voters (8,4)

indicators.note: take the last letter of slogan
N is taken in among the other letters
the voters' letters are unsettled, rearranged

annotation.surface: A text-speak protest banner waved by disillusioned Democrats.
annotation.walkthrough: In the definition, U is the old British label for upper-class, so 'I hate U' is a snob in reverse: someone who despises the posh.
annotation.definitionFit: An inverted snob looks down on the upper class, U in the old British shorthand.

entries.clue: One used to fighting old Prohibition (4)

blocks.note: a vet = a veteran, one used to fighting

annotation.surface: An old soldier who battled the ban on alcohol in 1920s America.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prohibition' looks like the American era; here it is just a ban.
annotation.definitionFit: A veto is a prohibition, a formal refusal to allow something.

entries.clue: Within limits, fancied backing fiery mount (4)

indicators.note: only what lies inside the outer letters is kept
the result goes backwards

annotation.surface: A rider backs a spirited horse, within reason.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mount' dresses as a steed in the surface; it is a mountain, the volcano on Sicily.
annotation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily, a mountain that breathes fire.

entries.clue: Contrary article edited a lot in The Times? (8)

indicators.note: contrary means facing the opposite way, so AN is turned round
A LOT IN is edited into a new order

blocks.note: an = indefinite article, reversed to NA

annotation.surface: A dissenting piece heavily rewritten before it appeared in the paper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' belongs to the anagram fodder, not a link. The Times is a British national newspaper, and the clue is set in it.
annotation.definitionFit: The Times is a national, a newspaper sold across the whole country.

entries.clue: Narcissus advanced, in a furtive manner, the last of his dodges (4,4)

indicators.note: SLILY dodges its S, leaving it out

blocks.note: slily, a variant spelling of slyly
last letter of hiS, removed from SLILY

annotation.surface: The vain youth of myth sidles forward, slipping away furtively.
annotation.walkthrough: Narcissus is the Greek youth in the surface but the flower genus in the answer; the Lent lily is the wild daffodil, blooming around Lent.
annotation.definitionFit: The Lent lily is the wild daffodil, a species of Narcissus.
